title: The definition drives execution: reordered, removed, added and re-addressed steps run exactly as the definition says
description: T-2808 (owner question: is the process a chain of functions called from code, or executed by the definition?). Runs in the platform tenant as the platform administrator with throwaway definitions uat-tmp-defproof-<run_id>-<n>; uses only platform.validate_registration, the notify step (mail and file) and no provisioner, no realm, no tenant creation. 1: A (validate, mail, file) and B (the same steps reordered) run in their own order; 2: C without the mail ends without mail; 3: D with a second catalogue function runs it once; 4: E sends another template to another recipient; 5: the instance of A stays on A after B is active; 6: an unknown function (refused at activate, 422 platform_calls_invalid / platform_call_function_unknown) and a dangling edge (refused at save, 422 dangling_edge) never reach a run. The step log of every instance is compared with the node order of its definition.

steps.says: The function picker of the designer (GET /api/v1/platform-functions) lists platform.validate_registration, the no-side-effect catalogue function this scenario uses (reads nothing, writes nothing).
The platform tenant's allow-list: the mail channel is open.
The catcher domain of the QA mail trap is allowed (the cleanup removes it again).
The file channel is open for the platform tenant.
1. Definition A (validate, hold for a person, mail, file) is saved as a draft under a throwaway name; the hold keeps the instance running while B is activated.
1. The designer's live check accepts A.
1. A is activated.
1. An instance of A is started by the definition's name.

steps.positional_ok: the list is filtered by this step's own query to the rows of this run; the first row is the one asked for
steps.says: 1. The instance of A stops at the hold: one PENDING task of node 'hold'.
1. While paused, the step log of A holds start and validate, A's first step.
1. Version b of the SAME definition: the same three steps REORDERED (file, validate, mail).
1. The live check accepts B.
1. B is activated (A is deprecated by it).
1. An instance of B is started by the same name.
1. The instance of B runs to its end.
1. The step log of B lists the steps in B's order (file, validate, mail), NOT in A's: the order is read from the definition.
1. B's mail is in the trap.
5. Version pinning: B is now the active version, and the still-running instance of A is ACTIVE and points at A's definition id.
5. The person claims A's hold task after B is active ...
5. ... and completes it.
5. The instance of A runs on to its end on A's graph, although B is active.
5. A's mail step (run after the switch to B) delivered: the trap holds the tenant_registered mail at A's recipient.
5. The instance started after the switch points at B.
5. The full step log of the first instance after B is active: A's order (validate, hold, mail, file).
2. Definition C: the mail step REMOVED (validate, file).
2. C is activated.
2. An instance of C is started.
2. The instance ends COMPLETED, without error.

2. The step log has no mail step at all (validate, file, end only) and every step is completed. The trap is not asked for 'no mail' (the runner has no absence check on the trap): the absence is proved by the log, which lists every visited node.

3. Definition D: a SECOND catalogue function (platform.validate_registration, picked from the catalogue) added after the first. The added call takes its own input slug2, so its idempotency key (function + slug) differs from the first call's.
3. D is activated.
3. An instance of D is started.
3. The instance of D ends COMPLETED.
3. The added function ran exactly once: one validate_again entry, completed, carrying the function name, between validate and mail; no sixth step.
4. Definition E: the mail step names ANOTHER template (password_reset_hint) and ANOTHER recipient variable (admin_email).
4. E is activated.
4. An instance of E is started with a recipient different from the registration e-mail.
4. The instance of E ends COMPLETED.
4. The step log lists validate, mail.
4. The trap holds THAT template ('Set a new password') at THAT recipient (the admin_email variable, not the registration e-mail).
6. A function that is not in the catalogue: the draft is saved (the function fence runs at activation, not at save).
6. Activating it is refused: 422 platform_calls_invalid, code platform_call_function_unknown. Nothing is switched on.
6. An instance cannot be started on the refused definition: no active version of that name (404).
6. An edge to a node that does not exist is refused at SAVE: 422 'definition graph failed validation', code dangling_edge. No draft exists, so it can never be activated or run.
6. Nothing of the refused definition reached a run: no active version of that name (404).

Sweep the throwaway definitions of EARLIER failed runs (T-2898): every definition whose name starts with uat-tmp-defproof- and does not contain this run's id is deleted through the product's own call (draft 204, active and deprecated 200, archived 409 / gone 404 accepted); one line per definition. A cleanup only knows its own ids, so without this a failed run leaves a draft that turns BP-PLATFORM-01 C4 red.
